\section[el castigo]{el castigo — the punishment}

\label{lesson:ES-C623-castigo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to force, then the Spanish for the obligation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el castigo}
\textbf{el castigo} — \textquotedblleft{}the punishment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El castigo fue muy duro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The punishment was very harsh.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Un castigo justo} — a fair punishment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{castigo} is built on \emph{castigar}, inherited from Latin \emph{castigare} 'to correct, to chastise', built on \emph{castus} 'pure' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el castigo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el castigo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el castigo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to force, then the Spanish for the obligation, then say \emph{el castigo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el castigo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The punishment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[castigar]{castigar — to punish}

\label{lesson:ES-C623-castigar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the obligation, then the Spanish for the punishment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: castigar}
\textbf{castigar} — \textquotedblleft{}to punish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Lo castigaron sin salir.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\emph{Castigar sin salir} — to keep a child in. Spelling: \emph{castigué}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{castigar} is inherited from Latin \emph{castigare} 'to correct, to chasten', built on \emph{castus} 'pure' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[la sanción]{la sanción — the penalty, the sanction}

\label{lesson:ES-C623-sancion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the punishment, then the Spanish for to punish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la sanción}
\textbf{la sanción} — \textquotedblleft{}the penalty, the sanction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El club recibió una sanción.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The club received a sanction.}
\end{quote}

A formal word for a punishment or fine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sanción} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sanctio} 'a decree, the penalty clause of a law', built on \emph{sancire} 'to make sacred, to decree' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sanción}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sanción}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la sanción}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the punishment, then the Spanish for to punish, then say \emph{la sanción} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[sancionar]{sancionar — to penalise, to sanction}

\label{lesson:ES-C623-sancionar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to punish, then the Spanish for the penalty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sancionar}
\textbf{sancionar} — \textquotedblleft{}to penalise, to sanction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La empresa fue sancionada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The company was penalised.}
\end{quote}

Common in the news, often in the passive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sancionar} is built on \emph{sanción}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sanctio} 'a decree', from \emph{sancire} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[multar]{multar — to fine}

\label{lesson:ES-C623-multar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the penalty, then the Spanish for to penalise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: multar}
\textbf{multar} — \textquotedblleft{}to fine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me multaron por ir rápido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They fined me for speeding.}
\end{quote}

The noun is \emph{la multa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{multar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{multare} 'to punish, to fine', built on \emph{multa} 'a fine' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Repaso de los capítulos 616–623}

\label{lesson:ES-R623-repaso-616-623}



\begin{quote}
Say the Spanish for the unexpected problem and to bring forward.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the unexpected problem, to bring forward, to postpone, the setback, the alternative
  \item the decision, the option, the dilemma, the priority, the criterion
  \item to imagine, the hypothesis, in theory, possibly, most likely
  \item maybe, predictable, the opportunity, the prospect, to predict
  \item the solution, to solve, the obstacle, complicated, to raise
  \item to stop, to make easier, to make difficult, exempt, forbidden
  \item the set of rules, the regulations, the ban, to force, the obligation
  \item the punishment, to punish, the penalty, to penalise, to fine
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The unexpected problem? (\textbf{el imprevisto}.) To bring forward? (\textbf{anticipar}.) To postpone? (\textbf{posponer}.) The setback? (\textbf{el contratiempo}.) The alternative? (\textbf{la alternativa}.) The decision? (\textbf{la decisión}.) The option? (\textbf{la opción}.) The dilemma? (\textbf{el dilema}.) The priority? (\textbf{la prioridad}.) The criterion? (\textbf{el criterio}.) To imagine? (\textbf{imaginar}.) The hypothesis? (\textbf{la hipótesis}.) In theory? (\textbf{en teoría}.) Possibly? (\textbf{posiblemente}.) Most likely? (\textbf{seguramente}.) Maybe? (\textbf{a lo mejor}.) Predictable? (\textbf{previsible}.) The opportunity? (\textbf{la oportunidad}.) The prospect? (\textbf{la perspectiva}.) To predict? (\textbf{predecir}.) The solution? (\textbf{la solución}.) To solve? (\textbf{solucionar}.) The obstacle? (\textbf{el obstáculo}.) Complicated? (\textbf{complicado}.) To raise? (\textbf{plantear}.) To stop? (\textbf{impedir}.) To make easier? (\textbf{facilitar}.) To make difficult? (\textbf{dificultar}.) Exempt? (\textbf{exento}.) Forbidden? (\textbf{prohibido}.) The set of rules? (\textbf{la normativa}.) The regulations? (\textbf{el reglamento}.) The ban? (\textbf{la prohibición}.) To force? (\textbf{obligar}.) The obligation? (\textbf{la obligación}.) The punishment? (\textbf{el castigo}.) To punish? (\textbf{castigar}.) The penalty? (\textbf{la sanción}.) To penalise? (\textbf{sancionar}.) To fine? (\textbf{multar}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
